newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain wise men revise growth, consumption forecast.
newsitem.headline: Spain wise men revise growth, consumption forecast.

text.p: Spain's wise men on Wednesday revised up their forecasts for 1997 economic growth and private consumption versus their previous January forecasts.
"...growth in GDP this year, for which the prior forecast was 2.9 percent, is now raised to 3.2 percent," the report published today said.
The group of experts who advise the Economy Ministry added that private consumption was likely to show stronger growth this year.

"...there are changes in the (internal demand and composition trend), the most important of which is private consumption, which is now seen growing 3.0 percent compared with 2.6 percent seen in January".
They added that forecast growth in domestic demand remained unchanged at 2.7 percent.
The wise men reiterated that the public deficit will meet the government's target of three percent of gross domestic product this year.
"..regarding the public deficit the average the group forecasts for 1997 is 3.0 percent, with very little divergence among them," the report wrote.

According to the experts, sustained international growth and economic stability are producing an "accelerated dynamic in internal demand which, together with a good rate of growth in exports, boosted GDP growth in the first months of the year, compatible with an improvement in the macroeconomic imbalance".
Despite the improvement in consumption, the wise men ruled out that Spain was in the face of a consumer boom. For 1998 they forecast 3.2 percent growth in consumption.
They also revised their consumer price index rate. Inflation should be 1.8 percent year on year in December 1997, to end 1998 at 2.2 percent.
The previous forecast expected the rate to end 1998 at 2.6 percent.
